title: From monodromy to $q$-monodromy
html:
Remark. From monodromy to q-monodromy

Classical local systems correspond to representations of \pi_1(X) because their connections satisfy d^2 = 0. In a quantum observable universe, the perpetual curvature d_q^2 \neq 0 (non-vanishing of d_q^2) obstructs naive flatness. The q-monodromy condition absorbs this obstruction. For contractible loops, parallel transport deviates from the identity by a residue proportional to (q-1).

The Kummer filtration measures this deviation at finite levels. An obstruction class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) vanishes modulo n precisely when n \mid \chi(A) (Kummer filtration). At these levels, the q-monodromy becomes n-divisible, determining a sublocus of \mathrm{LocSys}_{G_q}(X) with enhanced lifting properties through the brane tower. When n \nmid \chi(A), the obstruction forces a non-trivial q-holonomy residue on every q-local system. This behavior mirrors the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0, where the symmetric group relation (T-1)(T+1) = 0 deforms to split braiding eigenvalues from \pm 1 to q and -q^{-1}.
